evals.prompt: I'm helping a candidate prep for an interview and I have everything you need. ROLE: Senior GTM Strategy Lead, Emerging Products at Northwind Data (B2B data-infrastructure SaaS, ~3,000 employees). JD highlights: own GTM strategy for two new product lines; identify whitespace across land/adopt/expand/renew; run independent analysis in SQL and Tableau; partner-motion design experience required; strong cross-functional influence; AI experience a plus. CANDIDATE (call her Priya): 11 years — 2 years strategy consulting at a top firm, then 9 at a large consumer-tech company in product strategy & ops; built a partner-level revenue model used in carrier negotiations; set annual volume targets with cross-org consensus; proposed a store-surface change credited with a ~$400M ARR uplift; skilled in SQL/Tableau; uses AI tools daily. No classic sales-ops or quota-setting experience. INTERVIEWER: Dan Kovac, Director of Sales Strategy at Northwind — he would be Priya's PEER, both reporting to the same VP. His profile self-describes as 'relentlessly data-driven'; career spine is pricing and monetization roles, with one early-stage-startup chapter. RESEARCH NOTE I already did: Northwind's three stated priorities are enterprise expansion, an AI copilot launch ('Compass'), and reaching profitability; main competitive threat is bundling by a much larger platform vendor. This is a single 60-minute conversation with Dan. Please build the full mock-interview pack: questions categorized by interviewer persona and by question type, tabular, with answer guidance and the rationale for including and categorizing each question.
evals.expected_output: A complete markdown prep pack generated without any clarifying questions, with peer-weighted personas, grounded guidance mapped to Priya's stated stories, and every question carrying type tags, rationale, and a provenance label.
expectations: No clarifying question is asked before generating (round type, relationship, JD, and CV context were all supplied)
The output is a markdown pack containing persona-organized question-bank tables with columns covering the question, a type tag, answer guidance, and a rationale

A Peer Evaluator persona appears with elevated likelihood explicitly justified by the stated peer relationship, and its bank includes at least one seam/boundary question and one credit-sharing or reciprocity question

A Data-Driven Prober persona is weighted up with reasoning that cites Dan's 'data-driven' self-description, and at least one question asks Priya to defend the ~$400M ARR claim including her personal attribution

The fit snapshot maps the stated JD requirements to Priya's evidence and treats quota-setting/sales-ops as an explicit gap with bridge language, and at least one Skeptic or Pressure question rehearses that exact objection
At least one case or company question is grounded in the supplied research note (Compass launch, profitability push, or the bundling threat) rather than generic strategy
Every question's rationale ends with a provenance label ([grounded], [inferred], or [generic])
The pack ends with an upgrade menu listing concrete missing inputs (e.g., full JD text, full CV document, Dan's full profile) and what each unlocks
The pack explicitly states that the company's published values and documented interview process could not be established from attributable sources, rather than silently omitting the values section

evals.prompt: Interview next week, help me prep. The JD says: 'Operations Manager, Atlas Freight (regional logistics, 800 employees). Own daily terminal operations across 4 sites; drive on-time performance and cost-per-shipment down; lead a team of 12 supervisors; build reporting in Excel/Power BI; 5+ years operations leadership required; Lean/Six Sigma a plus.' My background: 7 years in warehouse and distribution ops, currently a senior shift manager over 3 supervisors; cut mis-pick rate 40% by redesigning the pick path; ran the site's peak-season surge plan two years running; green belt certified; solid Excel, never used Power BI. That's all I have — I don't know anything about who's interviewing me.
evals.expected_output: One compact clarifying exchange (round type + research consent), then a full pack that degrades honestly: no interviewer-read section, round-type persona priors, generic reverse questions, and an upgrade menu.
expectations: Exactly one clarifying message is sent before generating, containing at most three questions, covering round type/relationship to the interviewer and research-depth consent — and generation proceeds even though interviewer identity remains unknown
No 'Reading the interviewer' section appears in the pack, and no facts about any specific interviewer are invented
Reverse questions are role-generic (about the team, the sites, success criteria) with no fabricated references to a named interviewer

Each stated JD requirement (multi-site operations, on-time/cost metrics, team of 12, Power BI, Lean/Six Sigma) has at least one JD-tagged question, and the 3-supervisors-to-12 and Power BI gaps each get a Skeptic or Pressure question with bridge guidance
The 40% mis-pick claim gets a defend-the-number EXP question whose guidance includes naming the weakest assumption and precise personal attribution
The upgrade menu lists interviewer identity/profile and company research among the unlocks
The pack explicitly states that the company's published values and interview process could not be established from attributable sources, and names the archetype its loop assumptions fall back to

evals.prompt: I have a final-round interview at Stripe for a Product Operations Manager role. Help me get ready.
evals.expected_output: One bundled clarifying exchange, L1 research actually performed (official values/principles, documented loop structure), then an honest gate-only pack: inferred JD questions, a self-assessment fit worksheet, and heavy provenance labeling.
expectations: At most one clarifying message is sent (covering round detail/relationship, an offer to paste the JD and CV, and research-depth consent), and the pack is generated after that single exchange even if the user supplies nothing further

Web research is actually performed for Stripe's published operating principles/values and its documented interview process rather than answering from model memory, and the Sources section cites what was found
JD-derived questions are labeled [inferred] and the pack states they were built from a researched representative JD for the title
With no CV provided, the fit snapshot appears as a self-assessment worksheet variant with story-selection scaffolds instead of story-mapped guidance
A values/behavioral bank maps questions to the company's actual published principles found in research, by name
The pack ends with an upgrade menu, and no section fabricates a specific interviewer, team, or unverified company fact

The pack states that the final round is typically multiple sessions, runs as a single blended session-mode pack rather than fabricating a per-session schedule, and offers per-session packs in the upgrade menu once the schedule is known
